r.description: Ignore pink arrows this is another trail, Circular trail, Roman Road, Iron Age lynchets, Mature woodland, Roman signpost, Dog friendly, Picnic Spot, 'Six-Ways' signpost, Tree management

r.name: Hat Hill to Levin Down walk, Drovers Estate
Petworth Ancient Trees Walk, Petworth
r.description: Petworth has some of the countrys oldest & most venerable beeches, limes & oaks, including 1 that dates to the Norman Conquest. Discover more about the trees that dominate the Petworth skyline on this hilly circular. Some steep inclines, mud & unevenness.

r.name: Petworth Park Through Turner's Eyes, Petworth
r.description: Inspired by landscape painter, JMW Turner, who frequented Petworth thanks to the Earl of Egremont. Stroll round the lake & view scenes captured in his paintings. Stop at the house to see the largest Turner collection outside the Tate. Steep/uneven & steps

r.name: Capability Brown's Pleasure Gardens walk, Petworth
r.description: 1mile circular round the Pleasure Garden, past monuments added as part of the redevelopment of the garden in the late 18th Century by Capability Brown. Surfaced, grass and gravel paths with some gentle slopes and inclines. Muddy in wet weather.

r.name: Capability Brown's Parkland Walk, Petworth
r.description: 3-mile (4.8km) walk through the 700 acres (2.8sq km) of parkland sculpted by Lancelot 'Capability' Brown, with breath-taking views over the park to distant hills towards the South Downs. Gentle route with ascents. Dogs welcome under close control.

r.name: Woolbeding, River Rother and Midhurst Walk, South Downs West
r.description: Woolbeding Estate is a countryside gem, near Midhurst. Take in the beauty of the parkland. Follow the River Rother, edged with ancient trees. Pass a poplar plantation & hear the sounds of the weir before returning to the main street for its cafe's & pubs.
